provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no comma after quaesumus; 1962 has 'quaesumus, Domine'; 1862 sets a comma after Domine where 1962 sets a colon; 1862 sets a comma after 'pacifice nobis'; 1962 has none; 1862 sets a colon before 'et Ecclesia' where 1962 sets a semicolon; 1862 conclusion is the short cue 'Per Dominum.'; 1962 prints 'Per Dominum nostrum.'; OCR defects resolved in the 1862 layer, not textual: the ornamental initial mangled to 'TvA' for Da, 'pacffice' for pacifice, and laetetur reading 'laet&ur' at 48451 with one letter dropped mid-word. Corroboration: Venice 1570 at text-layer line 51431 prints 'tranquilla deuotione letetur' at exactly this point in its own Dominica IV formulary (lines 51427-51432), supplying the letter the 1862 lost. Degraded-latin OCR, corroboration only.. Recorded limitation: Marked medium for one reason and one only: the 1862 layer's 'laet&ur' drops a letter inside laetetur. The 1570 supplies the word at the same place in the same prayer, which is the tolerance the brief allows, and the gap is recorded rather than silently repaired. Everything else is pointing. Target text is given in the project's calendar rendering: unaccented, ae/oe expanded to two letters, printed line wraps joined, and the typica's i normalised to the project's j where it occurs. The typica itself prints no j in this prayer. That normalisation is the project's standing practice (src/sources/calendars/roman-1962/propers.yaml records it in terms at lines 20439, 43595 and 43622).
